findings.scenario: The sync driver has no per-row error containment: an arv.outbox row whose payload is not valid JSON (or is valid JSON missing the command's required fields, or contains newlines) — accepted by the substrate, which validates no payload shape at INSERT — crashes the walk with an UNHANDLED traceback (json.decoder.JSONDecodeError at sync.py's _cli_args json.loads), no named code, no repair line, violating the repo's own diagnostics contract. Because the crash happens AFTER the delivered-mark and the row rests in the non-terminal 'delivered' state, EVERY subsequent pass re-reads it, increments attempts, and dies at the same row: all later rows in seq order are permanently blocked (the owner's sync arm is unavailable until the row is manually repaired at the substrate). Reachable by the same hostile direct-SQL actor class SYN-11 itself defends against (arv_app INSERT or superuser), and by any future writer bug or payload corruption; NOT producible through the current CLI (commands.py always json.dumps the payload).
findings.evidence: My scratch rig (arv_sevloc_28044_879024946): (1) psql -U arv_app INSERT INTO arv.outbox (... payload 'not-json-at-all' ... state 'pending') -> accepted (rc=0); (2) python3 harness/sync.py sync --owner A --server-db arv_sevsrv_28044_879025006 -> rc=1 with 'Traceback (most recent call last): ... json.decoder.JSONDecodeError: Expecting value: line 1 column 1 (char 0)' and the earlier row acknowledged then the walk dead; (3) a NEW legitimate note (key sev-block1) created afterward stayed 'pending' with the server carrying 0 copies across two further sync attempts, while the poison row climbed attempts 3->4 in state 'delivered'.

findings.scenario: The identity bridge translates a referenced local id through the server's recorded answer for the creating command's key WITHOUT verifying that the answer belongs to the same logical command. After a 409 divergence on the creator (the server carries a DIFFERENT body under the same key — SYN-07's own scenario), every REFERENCER of that entity is delivered against the WRONG server entity (the competing body's entity) and its outbox row is stamped 'acknowledged' with the server's ref — a silent structural divergence between the local journal and the server state that no row, code, or sweep names. This falsifies the driver's own declared invariant ('translates a referenced local id to the server's id for the SAME logical entity'; '_refs_args': 'never a wrong-id delivery') in a composition built entirely from declared-matrix ingredients (a 409 conflict plus the natural next command of any real capture stream), and breaks SYS-08's user-validation equality ('the server ends with the same set the local journal shows') in a way SYN-15's key-set sweep cannot detect (the key sets still match; only the entity structure diverges). Repair direction: translate a referenced id only through a creating command whose LOCAL outbox row rests in 'acknowledged' (and/or verify the server's recorded answer corresponds to the local body under the translation), otherwise surface the named ordering-dependency/conflict refusal — never deliver against a conflicted key's answer.
findings.evidence: Two independent live demonstrations on my scratch rig. (A) Work-id variant (owner V): local import#1 key sev-v1 --title 'The Fallback Corpus' (three.txt), a hostile server-side competing import under the SAME key (four.txt, --title 'The Competing Corpus', rc=0), then local import#2 --work-id <local work>. Sync: sev-v1 -> failed ARV-CMD-409 (correct), but sev-v2 -> acknowledged; the server's source for sev-v2 belongs to work 'The Competing Corpus' while the local truth has it under 'The Fallback Corpus' (verified via arv_read joins on both dbs; the server even ends with two sources of the same digest). (B) Reference-target variant (owner Z): local highlight key sev-z1 span 4-9, a hostile server-side competing highlight under the same key span 5-9 (rc=0), then a local note --ref highlight:<local-id>@1. Sync: sev-z1 -> failed ARV-CMD-409 (correct), but the note -> acknowledged with its server note_reference row pointing at the COMPETING highlight's id (01a1ab8d-80c2-..., span 5-9) instead of the logical highlight the local journal references (span 4-9).

findings.scenario: The work-id fallback in sync.py's _cli_args (['--work-id', _translate_work(...) or p['work_id']]) passes the RAW LOCAL work id across the domain boundary when the work translation fails (the work's creating import terminally failed before ever delivering). The server-side ARV-CAP-006 existence check defends (zero effect, row retryable), so no wrong delivery lands — but the surfaced reason is the misleading 'work does not exist in the caller's scope' class instead of the named ARV-SYN-009 ordering dependency, contradicting the driver's own no-raw-id law in letter, and the pattern would silently attach to a wrong work in the (negligible-probability) event of a cross-domain id collision. findings.scenario: The substrate's enforced transition graph is a permissive superset of RTM §3.4's declared graph: every RTM edge is enforced (verified by reading + the hostile probes), but the migration additionally allows pending->failed, delivered->failed, uncertain->delivered, retryable->delivered, delivered->delivered and retryable->retryable. The cycles are the driver's own re-drive mechanics (the delivered-mark precedes every send); delivered->failed and uncertain->delivered are driver-reachable; pending->failed is reachable ONLY by a hostile/direct writer (the driver always passes through delivered first) and lets such a writer terminally suppress a not-yet-delivered row (the row survives, visible as failed with a NULL-able reason — SYN-15's sweep would flag the reason-less form). A documentation-alignment item: RTM §3.4's compressed graph, the migration header's declared graph, and the enforced graph should be reconciled in one place. Revisit condition: the RTM refresh at the next §3.4 touch or any P4 state-machine extension.

review_summary: Fresh-context SEV of CLAIM-059 / P3-08 (the local outbox, the sync driver, the recovery semantics) over the diff 67e37fa...2a209c5 (digest 90acf920...). The slice's pinned claims reproduce on my own two-database scratch rig: the SYN-01..15 suite exits 0 with output byte-identical to the recorded runs; the atomic enqueue, the replay/duplicate/out-of-order/409/outage/death-window/cross-owner matrix, the substrate guard set (ARV-SYN-004/005/006/007/008/010 all re-fired by name under my own superuser probes), the D-018 handoff, the work-id bridge and the creator preference all verified live; the red-first trail is genuine (the RED form's digest matches the record, and I reproduced the ARV-TEST-000 failure in a clone at e91dc9a); LAW-05 holds by my own count (381/400 source, 686/800 test, 1 migration). TWO findings block merge. F2 (P0): the identity bridge — this slice's core novel mechanism — translates referenced ids through the server's answer for the creating command's key without checking that the answer belongs to the same logical command; after a 409 divergence on a creator (SYN-07's own scenario), referencers are delivered against the WRONG server entity and stamped 'acknowledged' — demonstrated live in both the work-id variant (an import attached to the competing import's work) and the reference-target variant (a note's server reference pointing at the competing highlight) — a silent structural divergence that falsifies the driver's own 'SAME logical entity / never a wrong-id delivery' invariant and that SYN-15's key-set sweep cannot detect. F1 (P1): the driver has no per-row error containment — a hostile or corrupted outbox payload (accepted by the substrate, which validates no payload shape) crashes the walk with an unhandled traceback and permanently blocks every later row in every subsequent pass. F3-F6 are routed P2s (the raw work-id fallback, the transition-graph superset vs RTM §3.4, the per-attempt temp-file leak, the stale scratch-database disclosure in notverified.txt). Disposition BLOCKED: repair F2 (translate only through creators whose local outbox rows rest acknowledged, or verify the server answer's correspondence) and F1 (contain per-row parse/shape errors as a named failed/retryable outcome and continue the walk), then re-run the SEV chain over the repaired diff.
